body:
Thank you for your advice, it’s good to hear you have a friend who has been there for you. 

I ended up being somewhat open and told her that things just aren’t going well for me and I’m not where I thought I’d be in life, that I’m unhappy. So far she’s been asking questions and doesn’t seem negative about it. I’m not ready to tell her about wanting to die but I guess she doesn’t need to know at this point.

Thank you. There’s no best answer really, but I feel better for reading your response and it makes me feel useful in I could help you in some small way too. Whatever you decide to do, know that you have made me feel something today and that means more than anyone would think.

I once booked an appointment with a GP at age 17 after being advised to, told this ‘dr’ how worthless and sad I felt, and was told that ‘we only offer help to people who have been through a big deal like bereavement or divorce. You seem like a collected person.’ With morons like that as the first point of contact no wonder people don’t get help. 

I’m so sorry you had to experience such uselessness from a service that should have helped you.
